slides.say: a and b are positive integers. Given: a is smaller than b, and a times b, plus four a, is equal to forty-eight. Which of the following cannot be the value of a plus b?

Look at the equation. a appears in both terms on the left. So we can take it out, and we get a product that is equal to forty-eight. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, taking out a and listing the pairs, and then checking the sum seventeen directly.
[short pause] Take out a. a times b, plus four a, is a times, in brackets, b plus four. And that's forty-eight.
So two whole numbers multiply to forty-eight. a is one of them, and b plus four is the other. They don't have to be primes.
Which one is a? The smaller one. Why? b is bigger than a, so b plus four is even bigger. For example, if a is three and b is five, b plus four is nine, bigger than three.

For every factor pair, the smaller factor is a and the larger factor is b plus four. We have to subtract four from that larger factor before finding the requested sum. So let's list the pairs that make forty-eight, the small number first. I'll write a, then b plus four, then b, then a plus b.
One times forty-eight. So b plus four is forty-eight, and b is forty-four. One plus forty-four is forty-five.
Two times twenty-four. b is twenty. Two plus twenty is twenty-two.
Three times sixteen. b is twelve. Three plus twelve is fifteen.
Four times twelve. b is eight. Four plus eight is twelve.

Five doesn't divide forty-eight. Six times eight. b plus four is eight, so b is four. But b has to be bigger than a, and four is smaller than six. Not allowed. After that the pairs swap, so we're done.
So the sum can be forty-five, twenty-two, fifteen or twelve. Seventeen is not on the list. Choice number three is our answer.
[pause] Another way is to check seventeen directly. If a plus b is seventeen, then b is seventeen minus a. So b plus four is twenty-one minus a.

And a times b plus four is forty-eight, so a divides forty-eight. Also a is smaller than b, so a is at most eight. The numbers up to eight that divide forty-eight are one, two, three, four, six and eight.

For each allowed a, the sum condition fixes b. We'll test a times the whole bracket b plus four, using twenty-one minus a for that bracket. Let's try each. a is one: one times twenty is twenty. a is two: two times nineteen is thirty-eight. a is three: three times eighteen is fifty-four.
a is four: four times seventeen is sixty-eight. a is six: six times fifteen is ninety. a is eight: eight times thirteen is a hundred four.
None of them is forty-eight. So the sum can't be seventeen. Choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
